seventh-day-adventism.1: Members get Bible studies at home, meals, hospital visits and a full-day Sabbath community.
seventh-day-adventism.2: The church network offers practical help: jobs in the system, school places, hospital access.
seventh-day-adventism.3: Prophetic certainty about a Sunday law has been imminent for a century and a half.
seventh-day-adventism.8: Assurance is offered and then qualified by the judgment, so peace is always provisional.
seventh-day-adventism.12: Glacier View is retold as a theologian's failure, not a doctrine's examination.
seventh-day-adventism.13: Fifty years without available transcripts are absorbed as normal archival practice.
seventh-day-adventism.15: Members compare each other on diet, dress and Sabbath strictness.
seventh-day-adventism.20: Judgment anxiety is relieved weekly by the same church's assurance teaching.
seventh-day-adventism.22: Health teaching that is genuinely good for you is enforced as righteousness.
seventh-day-adventism.23: Members are told historical and theological questions are for scholars, not for them.
seventh-day-adventism.24: Sabbath, diet, education, employment, marriage and social life all sit inside one system.
seventh-day-adventism.25: Depression is answered with diet, prayer and Bible study rather than treatment.
seventh-day-adventism.26: Tithe flows past the local congregation to the conference that employs the pastor.
seventh-day-adventism.27: The time of trouble and the Sunday law are presented as a permanent, imminent emergency.
seventh-day-adventism.28: Credentials are withdrawn for doctrinal dissent, and Glacier View is the named precedent.

anglicanism.1: It appears in some evangelical outreach, such as Alpha courses, but not in most parishes.
anglicanism.14: Historically, isolation happened in closed camps and choir environments.

christianity.16: The pastor does not confront; small-group leaders and "concerned friends" text instead.

hinduism.10: Caste may be called spiritual order, social custom or irrelevant ideal, depending on criticism.
hinduism.13: Ritual, caste expectations and purity rules feel normal because family life embeds them.

indigenous.8: Readings that land build the practitioner's reputation; ambiguous ones blame the client.

jainism.10: Dietary rules are called discipline, family expectation or purity, depending on audience.

judaism.7: Intermarriage or non-observance turns a questioner who wrestles into one who is lost.

pentecostal-charismatic.1: Newcomers get prayer by name, a ride home, a meal and an invitation to serve.
pentecostal-charismatic.3: A specific prophetic word says this year is yours and the business will open.
pentecostal-charismatic.7: Those who give beyond their means are praised; those who give less are quietly marked.
pentecostal-charismatic.13: Doors are closed during the offering, and givers are called forward by amount.
pentecostal-charismatic.15: Givers are compared in public: whoever sows at this level, come forward.
pentecostal-charismatic.23: Adult members are addressed as spiritual children, with no path to adult standing.
pentecostal-charismatic.26: Giving runs through seed faith, first fruits, prophetic offerings and building funds.
pentecostal-charismatic.27: Emergencies recur with deadlines: the property will be lost, the window closes Sunday.
pentecostal-charismatic.30: There is no membership roll, no minutes, no constitution and no published accounts.
pentecostal-charismatic.10: The call to "sow a significant seed" never defines "significant," so members compete upward.

sikhism.10: Visible identity may be called devotion, communal duty or family honor, depending on pressure.

unification-church.22: Marriage and life decisions are guided "for the lineage."
unification-church.30: The conduct is attributed to "individual members' excesses."
